chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who purchased food from another man with dirhams, took half of it, and left half, then came back later when the price of the food had risen or fallen: He (peace be upon him) said, 'If on the day of purchase he fixed the price for him saying,

key_terms.سَاعَرَهُ: he fixed the price for him

ai.seo_question: How is the price determined for a partial food purchase if the market price changes before the buyer takes the rest?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *s'ar* (market price) in partial sales, distinguishing between a fixed agreed valuation and a default current market rate. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in *bay'* (trade) by preventing exploitation during price volatility, ensuring the buyer pays only for the actual value of the portion retained. This ruling underscores the principle that uncertainty (*gharar*) is minimized when the transaction's financial basis is clearly defined at the time of agreement.
